aboutH2: The Residence at Homewood: Private Mental Health and Addiction Care in Guelph, Ontario
intro: The Residence at Homewood is a private mental health and addiction treatment center in Guelph, Ontario, known for its personalized, medically supervised care in a peaceful and confidential setting. Located on the spacious 50-acre campus of the respected Homewood Health Centre, it offers support to individuals dealing with anxiety, depression, trauma, PTSD, addiction, and burnout. Every person receives a treatment plan tailored to their specific needs, which may include therapy sessions, psychiatric support, innovative treatments like rTMS or ketamine therapy, and wellness activities such as yoga, fitness, mindfulness, and nutrition. Guests stay in comfortable, private rooms and enjoy meals prepared by in-house chefs, all within a calm, welcoming environment designed to promote healing. With a compassionate team of experienced professionals and a strong focus on personalized care, The Residence at Homewood offers a safe space where people can focus on their recovery and take meaningful steps toward a healthier life.

pillars.title: A 1903 House on the Homewood Campus in Guelph
pillars.body: The Residence is a red-brick Edwardian house built in 1903 as the home of Homewood's Medical Superintendent. It was restored under a plan announced in 2016 and sits in a wooded corner of the 50-acre Homewood campus at 148 Delhi Street in Guelph. There are only nine bedrooms, all private, and each has an ensuite marble bathroom, a desk and its own climate control. Shared spaces include a living room with a fireplace, a sun room, a wrap-around front porch and a patio with a barbecue, and the grounds have walking trails, gardens with a meditation labyrinth, and tennis and basketball courts. The house runs separately from Homewood Health Centre, the 300-bed hospital on the same campus.

pillars.title: A Year of Recovery Management After Discharge
pillars.body: Discharge planning starts while you are still in the house, and eligible clients meet their Recovery Management Therapist several times before going home. The centre describes one year of aftercare through its Recovery Management Program, made up of telephone check-ins, individual sessions and weekly groups such as Road to Recovery and Skills and Transition. Some groups run once a year, including an eight-week Mindfulness-Based Relapse Prevention course and a ten-week Healthy Living group. Graduates can also join the Homewood alumni program. One-to-one counselling, step-down programming and substance-use monitoring are available as paid extras, and eligibility for the program is confirmed at intake.

pillars.title: A Psychiatrist-Led Team With Nurses on Site Around the Clock
pillars.body: Care is led by Dr. Ben McCutchen, Chief of Psychiatry, and Dr. Rachel Lyon, a psychologist who serves as Clinical Lead. The wider team includes psychiatrists, addiction counsellors, a social worker, an occupational therapist, a recreation therapist, an art therapist and a strength and conditioning coach, and a nursing team is in the house 24 hours a day. With nine clients at most, people typically have 8 to 12 individual sessions a week with members of this team. Meals come from a culinary team led by an Executive Chef. If the client agrees, families can take part through family meetings and a named staff contact.

overviewH2: The Residence at Homewood: Centre Overview
overview: The Residence treats adults living with depression, including treatment-resistant depression, as well as anxiety, PTSD and other trauma, OCD, substance use and co-occurring conditions. It also offers a physician-led service for chronic pain and the mental health problems that often come with it. Because it shares a campus with Homewood Health Centre, clients can be referred to Homewood's Interventional Psychiatry Service for rTMS, ECT or intravenous pharmacological therapy at no extra cost when the treatment team decides it is medically indicated. Progress is tracked with Measurement-Based Care, where short questionnaires at intake and during the stay are used to adjust the plan as you go.

location.heading: The Residence at Homewood in Guelph, Ontario
location.intro: The Residence at Homewood is on the Homewood Health Centre campus in Guelph, a university city in Wellington County just west of the Greater Toronto Area. Downtown Toronto is about an hour and a quarter away by car and Toronto Pearson Airport about an hour, while Kitchener-Waterloo and Cambridge are roughly 25 to 30 minutes and Hamilton about 45 minutes.

cells.v: Self-referrals accepted, no doctor's note needed

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's listing and its own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: What does it cost, and do you accept insurance?
faqs.a: They recommend chatting with their intake team to get all the details. Costs vary based on your treatment plan, and you’ll want to ask about insurance coverage or payment options early on.

faqs.q: How long will I be there?
faqs.a: Typical program durations run between 45 and 52 days, although this can shift depending on your individual needs and treatment progress.

faqs.q: What does The Residence at Homewood treat?
faqs.a: The Residence treats depression (including treatment-resistant depression), anxiety, PTSD and other trauma, OCD, substance use and co-occurring disorders, along with more complex combinations of these. The centre also lists burnout, bipolar disorder and chronic pain with related mental health problems. Every plan starts from a multi-day assessment in the first week.

faqs.q: What kinds of treatment do you offer?
faqs.a: They provide a range of care, including intensive inpatient programs, detox services, and 1-on-1 counselling for issues like addiction, anxiety, depression, PTSD, OCD, and trauma.

faqs.q: Does The Residence at Homewood offer detox?
faqs.a: Yes. The centre lists medically supervised detox as part of its intensive inpatient program, and its substance use treatment includes medical detox management. Clients do need to be medically stable when they are admitted, so the intake team will go over your situation before you arrive.

faqs.q: Where is The Residence at Homewood located?
faqs.a: It’s right in Guelph, Ontario, nestled on a peaceful 50-acre campus alongside the well-regarded Homewood Health Centre.

faqs.q: How do I get to The Residence in Guelph?
faqs.a: The Residence is at 148 Delhi Street in Guelph, about an hour and a quarter by car from downtown Toronto. The centre says it is about an hour from Toronto Pearson Airport, 45 minutes from Hamilton's airport and 20 minutes from Region of Waterloo International Airport, and it can arrange transport from all three. Clients who drive get free on-site parking for their whole stay.

faqs.q: Is The Residence part of Homewood Health Centre?
faqs.a: It shares the 50-acre campus and the Homewood Health name, but The Residence is a separate private program with nine bedrooms. Homewood Health Centre next door is a 300-bed accredited Schedule 1 mental health hospital with its own programs. Residence clients can use some hospital services, such as the Interventional Psychiatry Service, and can book physiotherapy or osteopathy there for a fee.

Eligible clients get one year of aftercare through the Recovery Management Program. It includes telephone check-ins, individual sessions and weekly groups, plus longer courses such as Mindfulness-Based Relapse Prevention. You meet your Recovery Management Therapist before discharge, and you can join the Homewood alumni program.

faqs.q: Is this a private centre? Can I use my benefits?
faqs.a: Yes, The Residence is a private, self-pay program, and recovery.com lists it as private pay. The centre does not publish its fees or how it handles insurance claims. Ask the intake team at 1-877-290-3317 whether any part of your stay can be claimed through an employer or extended health plan.

faqs.q: Do I need a referral from my doctor?
faqs.a: No. The Residence accepts self-referrals as well as referrals from doctors, employers and other professionals. Clients must be 18 or older, medically stable and not a risk to themselves or others. The intake team can explain the admission process and the cost of treatment.

faqs.q: What should I bring with me?
faqs.a: Just the essentials are needed: Your provincial health card and photo ID; A few days’ supply of prescription meds; Weather-appropriate clothes; A few personal items to feel comfortable.
